events.body:
D1: The $6.61 was charged because the rider cancelled the trip herself 3 min 5 s after acceptance (17:12:00 → 17:15:05), i.e. beyond Ryde's 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the fee is validly triggered on the rider's own act of cancellation. [F2 F5] [NS-0 NS-4]
D2: The rider's stated reason — 'the driver was still far away' — is consistent with the record: the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 1725 m, so no no-show scenario under NS-1 ever arose and no counterclaim against the driver can be built on the arrival timeline. [F1 F3] [NS-1]
D3: No arrival confirmation exists on the record — the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' and the platform logged no automatic arrival — hence no waiting-fee or no-show fee was or could be imposed against the rider; the only sum on record is the cancellation fee of $6.61. [F4 F5] [NS-0 NS-1]
D4: The driver kept the rider informed: he replied 'Coming, about 5 min' at 17:13 to the rider's 17:12 query 'Are you near?', so the rider had a live estimate of the driver's position before she chose to cancel at 17:15:05. [F7 F8 F2] [NS-4]
D5: The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so the events can be reconstructed without any need to resort to the incompleteness rule; the driver's own statement is consistent with the log. [F9 F10] [NS-4]
D6: There is no ground to reduce or waive the fee on the driver's side: the record shows no traffic incidents and fair weather, and the driver had no arrival-button abuse, so nothing in NS-1/NS-2 is engaged against the driver. [F11 F12 F13 F4] [NS-2]
D7: The driver's record is clean — 1018 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld — so no account flag is warranted on this file and the cancellation fee should stand. [F15 F5] [NS-3 NS-4]

claims.assertion: The $6.61 was charged because the rider cancelled the trip herself 3 min 5 s after acceptance (17:12:00 → 17:15:05), i.e. beyond Ryde's 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the fee is validly triggered on the rider's own act of cancellation.

The rider's stated reason — 'the driver was still far away' — is consistent with the record: the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 1725 m, so no no-show scenario under NS-1 ever arose and no counterclaim against the driver can be built on the arrival timeline.

No arrival confirmation exists on the record — the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' and the platform logged no automatic arrival — hence no waiting-fee or no-show fee was or could be imposed against the rider; the only sum on record is the cancellation fee of $6.61.

The driver kept the rider informed: he replied 'Coming, about 5 min' at 17:13 to the rider's 17:12 query 'Are you near?', so the rider had a live estimate of the driver's position before she chose to cancel at 17:15:05.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so the events can be reconstructed without any need to resort to the incompleteness rule; the driver's own statement is consistent with the log.

There is no ground to reduce or waive the fee on the driver's side: the record shows no traffic incidents and fair weather, and the driver had no arrival-button abuse, so nothing in NS-1/NS-2 is engaged against the driver.
The driver's record is clean — 1018 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld — so no account flag is warranted on this file and the cancellation fee should stand.

weaknesses: The rider's core complaint — that the driver was 1725 m away and not arriving within a reasonable time (F1, F8) — cannot be answered: Ryde has no rule allowing the rider free cancellation on delay grounds (NS-8 is informational and un-citable), but the record plainly shows the driver was nowhere near the pickup at the moment of cancellation (F1, F3), so a judge may feel the $6.61 is harsh and lean on Ryde's discretion (NS-7) or send the file to a human.

The driver's own statement 'The rider cancelled while I was still on the way' (F10) openly admits he had not arrived; it is not contradicted by any system fact, but it does confirm the rider's version of the facts even though it does not shift the policy outcome.

Ryde does not publish any rule that a rider is free to cancel when the driver is late (NS-8 informational; no ETA field in the file), so my case rests purely on the 3-minute rule in NS-4 rather than on any positive service-quality defence.
The cancellation fee is only a recommendation of this system: NS-7 leaves Ryde absolute discretion and requires voucher form, so a favourable finding still may not be executed as charged (F5).

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The cancellation fee $6.61 can only stand if the driver pressed "I'm Here" (or the platform auto-confirmed arrival) and then waited over 3 minutes at the pickup point; here no arrival was ever confirmed, because driver_arrived_at is null and driver_pressed_here_at is null, so NS-1 (i) fails.
NS-1 (ii) also fails: the driver's closest approach to the Bedok Mall pickup was 1725 m at 17:15:05 and he never came within 200 m, so at no point was he at the pickup location according to GPS.
NS-1 (iii) fails as well: with no arrival tap and no time within 200 m of the pickup, there is no continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point before the cancellation (F2).
Because every NS-1 condition fails, the $6.61 charged cancellation fee must be refunded in full under NS-2; the amount is fixed by the fare record at $6.61 (F5), with no surge applied (F6).

The driver's own written statement confirms he had not reached the pickup point ("The rider cancelled while I was still on the way"), which is consistent with the GPS record that he never entered the 200 m pickup radius; either way the system records (F1, F3, F4) govern over this statement.

The driver's chat message at 17:13 estimated he was still "about 5 min" away, i.e. ETA ~17:18, so no arrival was possible before the rider cancelled at 17:15:05; Ryde publishes no free-cancellation rule for a late driver (NS-8 is informational), so the rider's route to relief is this fee-waiver dispute, filed within time.

The rider's cancellation was a reasonable reaction to a driver still ~1.7 km away, and the $6.61 is a self-serve fee-waiver item within the 30-day window payable as a Ryde voucher; the rider has no upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days (F14), so no rider-side flag is warranted.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance, which is just past the 3-minute mark; if the record instead showed a valid "I'm Here" tap at 17:12, the $6.61 could stand under NS-1 — I rely on F3 and F4 (no arrival confirmation) to defeat that.

The rider's message "Are you near?" (F7) and the driver's "Coming, about 5 min" (F8) show the rider knew the driver had not arrived; the other side may argue the rider chose to cancel rather than wait, though Ryde publishes no ETA-based free cancellation (NS-8 is informational, no ETA field in the file).

No GPS samples between 17:12 and 17:15 are in the fact table other than the closest-approach figure (F1); the driver may argue there was a GPS gap, but the record as given shows he never came within 200 m, and any gap would only move the case to manual review, not help him.
The driver's 1018 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes (F15) may be used to argue he is a reliable operator; profile facts cannot decide the case (and equally cannot rescue the missing NS-1 conditions).

claims.assertion: The $6.61 was charged because the rider cancelled the trip herself 3 min 5 s after acceptance (17:12:00 → 17:15:05), i.e. beyond Ryde's 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the fee is validly triggered on the rider's own act of cancellation.

The rider's stated reason — 'the driver was still far away' — is consistent with the record: the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 1725 m, so no no-show scenario under NS-1 ever arose and no counterclaim against the driver can be built on the arrival timeline.

No arrival confirmation exists on the record — the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' and the platform logged no automatic arrival — hence no waiting-fee or no-show fee was or could be imposed against the rider; the only sum on record is the cancellation fee of $6.61.

The driver kept the rider informed: he replied 'Coming, about 5 min' at 17:13 to the rider's 17:12 query 'Are you near?', so the rider had a live estimate of the driver's position before she chose to cancel at 17:15:05.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so the events can be reconstructed without any need to resort to the incompleteness rule; the driver's own statement is consistent with the log.

There is no ground to reduce or waive the fee on the driver's side: the record shows no traffic incidents and fair weather, and the driver had no arrival-button abuse, so nothing in NS-1/NS-2 is engaged against the driver.
The driver's record is clean — 1018 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld — so no account flag is warranted on this file and the cancellation fee should stand.

weaknesses: The rider's core complaint — that the driver was 1725 m away and not arriving within a reasonable time (F1, F8) — cannot be answered: Ryde has no rule allowing the rider free cancellation on delay grounds (NS-8 is informational and un-citable), but the record plainly shows the driver was nowhere near the pickup at the moment of cancellation (F1, F3), so a judge may feel the $6.61 is harsh and lean on Ryde's discretion (NS-7) or send the file to a human.

The driver's own statement 'The rider cancelled while I was still on the way' (F10) openly admits he had not arrived; it is not contradicted by any system fact, but it does confirm the rider's version of the facts even though it does not shift the policy outcome.

Ryde does not publish any rule that a rider is free to cancel when the driver is late (NS-8 informational; no ETA field in the file), so my case rests purely on the 3-minute rule in NS-4 rather than on any positive service-quality defence.
The cancellation fee is only a recommendation of this system: NS-7 leaves Ryde absolute discretion and requires voucher form, so a favourable finding still may not be executed as charged (F5).

points.response: I accept the arithmetic and the trigger, but the rider-side 3-minute rule in NS-4 is not the applicable branch: the fee only exists because the rider cancelled, and NS-0 requires the reasonableness of the charge to be tested — the driver's own record (F1, F3, F4) shows he was nowhere near the pickup and had not confirmed arrival, so the fee stands only if Ryde chooses to keep it despite the rider's cancellation being driven by non-arrival.

D2 concedes the decisive facts: the driver's closest approach was 1725 m (F1) and no arrival was ever recorded (F3, F4), so NS-1 has no possible application in the driver's favour — the $6.61 cannot be justified as a no-show fee, only as a timing-based cancellation charge.

This is my case: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was logged (F4), so NS-1 (i) and (ii) both fail and NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full, sized by the fare record (F5).

The "about 5 min" reply (F8) at 17:13 is an admission the driver needed until roughly 17:18, i.e. he could not have reached the pickup before the 17:15:05 cancellation (F2); it therefore corroborates non-arrival rather than excusing the charge.

The complete, timestamped chat (F9) is exactly what allows the timeline to be read: at 17:15:05 the driver was still 1725 m out (F1) and had given an ETA he had not met (F8), so no NS-1 condition is met at the moment of cancellation.

I do not seek a driver-side no-show finding and I do not rely on traffic or weather (F11 band 4, F12 no incidents, F13 fair weather); my case is that the rider-side charge is unsupported because NS-1 was never satisfied (F4), which is precisely what NS-2 addresses.

I do not ask for a flag_account against the driver, and his 1018 trips with 0 disputes (F15) is not in issue; but nothing in NS-3/NS-4 makes the rider's $6.61 valid when the arrival conditions of NS-1 are absent (F4), and NS-7 says the refund is a Ryde voucher.

Conceded on the fact, contested on the law: it is true that no arrival was confirmed (F3, F4), but that defeats a $6.61 no-show/waiting charge against the rider — it does not defeat a cancellation fee, which Ryde charges by reference to cancelled_by and the 3-minute window (F2).

Accept the fact: the closest approach was 1725 m and the 200 m radius was never entered (F1), so NS-1 (ii) cannot be satisfied — but NS-1 only governs a driver-cancelled no-show fee, and here the rider cancelled (F2), so NS-4 not NS-1 sets the outcome.
Agreed that no waiting period can be shown (F1, F2); the waiting conditions in NS-1 are simply inapplicable because the rider — not the driver — cancelled the trip (F2).

This is the circle the rider's case runs in: NS-2 only applies when the driver cancels and claims a no-show, which never happened (F2), so the refund claim under NS-2 fails; the rider's own cancellation 3 min 5 s after acceptance (17:12:00 → 17:15:05) falls outside the 3-minute free window of NS-4 and the fee stands.

The statement (F10) is not disputed and the system records (F1, F3, F4) confirm only that the driver was en route; none of these facts engage a driver-side obligation, because the driver neither cancelled nor tapped 'I'm Here' and no charge was levied against the rider for waiting or no-show.

The driver's 'about 5 min' at 17:13 (F8) is the very reason there is no ETA-based waiver: Ryde publishes no free-cancellation rule for a late driver (NS-8 is informational) and no ETA field exists in the file, so a 3-minute overrun of the free window is still a chargeable cancellation under NS-4.

The rider's reaction may well have been reasonable in ordinary terms, but NS-4 charges the fee by the clock, not by sympathy, and the clock shows 3 min 5 s (F2); the driver's clean record of 1018 trips with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F15) supports leaving the fee intact with no flag.
